title: A Cedar policy decides one call
lede: A Cedar AI policy can refuse a tool call, hold it for a human, or withhold content from a reply, using caller, tool, argument and scope facts.

steps.title: The facts a rule can read
steps.what: The editor exposes the caller, the tool and its named arguments, the app, token and key scopes, approvals so far and AI Guard findings.
steps.why: Cedar reading PingFederate token scopes was measured on one PingFederate-token door only and should not be generalised.

steps.title: Permit, hold or refuse
steps.what: A policy can refuse a call, hold it for a human, or withhold content from a model reply; hold annotations set grant and request lifetime, approvers and reason.
steps.why: Denials and holds are written to the gateway log.

steps.title: Candidate until Active
steps.what: A policy is Candidate (validated, stored, never enforced) or Active (enforced); an API-created policy stays empty until set Active.
steps.why: App and policy edits take about 4 minutes to reach the gateway.
